title: ScheduledService

service_id.description: ID of the service to be triggered

rrule.description: Recurrence rule for recurring scheduled services, e.g. 'FREQ=MONTHLY' or 'FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2'; see [RFC2445](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2445#section-4.3.10).

timezone_id.description: Timezone ID used to compute times for recurring scheduled services; see [List of tz database time zones Wikipedia article](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones).

time_created.description: Time the scheduled service was created in Telerivet

start_time.description: The time that the service will be triggered (or first triggered for recurring scheduled services)

end_time.description: Time after which a recurring scheduled service will stop (not applicable to non-recurring scheduled services)

prev_time.description: The most recent time that Telerivet triggered this scheduled service (null if it has never been triggered)

next_time.description: The next upcoming time that Telerivet will trigger this scheduled service (null if it will not be triggered again)

occurrences.description: Number of times this scheduled service has already been triggered

vars.description:
Custom variables stored for this scheduled service. Variable names may be up to 32 characters in length and can contain the characters a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and _.
 Values may be strings, numbers, or boolean (true/false).
 String values may be up to 4096 bytes in length when encoded as UTF-8.
 Up to 100 variables are supported per object.
 Setting a variable to null will delete the variable.

project_id.description: ID of the project this scheduled service belongs to

description:
Represents a scheduled service within Telerivet.

 Scheduled services allow services to be triggered automatically at specified times.
 The ScheduledService object is only used for services that are triggered for a project (e.g. `scheduled_actions` or `scheduled_script`).

 Note: To schedule services that are triggered for a contact, the ScheduledMessage object should be used instead, with `message_type`=`service`.
